Subject: Procurement acceptance rules and invoice rhythm for Sygnus Labs

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to capture the hard requirements so we can start drafting the PO. Two quick asks on your side before we build the internal purchase order:

- Required PO fields (customer PO should reference what fields so our ERP maps correctly: account code, BU, cost center, PO line IDs?).
- Preferred invoice cadence: do you support monthly consolidated invoices or do you need per-PO/per-entity invoices?
- Net terms options and any discount/commitment thresholds tied to net terms (e.g., net30 vs net45 and associated pricing tiers).

We also need your standard PO template and the pricing worksheet you used in the proposal so we can attach to the request. Ideally we need this by EOD Thursday to keep internal routing on track for a Nov subscription start.

Alicia

Subject: Re: Procurement acceptance rules and invoice rhythm for Sygnus Labs

Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and I attached the two files you asked for.

- PO fields: we require PO number, legal entity, billing entity, remit-to address, BU code (if you use internal BU codes we can map a free-text field), a line-level SKU/description, and the service start date. We also ask for a single mapping field named "PO reference" which we echo on invoice lines for ERP matching.
- Invoice cadence: our standard is monthly consolidated invoices per billing entity. We can do per-PO invoices but that adds ~15% operational surcharge unless you commit to a minimum monthly invoice count. If you need weekly or biweekly runs we can support with an ops fee and lead time.
- Net terms and discounts: base pricing is listed in the attached pricing_grid_v3.xlsx. Net30 is standard; Net45 is available at a 2% reduction on list for orders > $100k ARR; Net60 would require credit approval and either a prepay or a 4% discount. We can also offer a 1% early-pay discount if you pay within 10 days.

I've looped in Vivek from finance for any credit/Net60 exceptions, and Vanessa who will own the SOW + consolidation.

Next steps suggestion: 1) you confirm the billing entity and target invoice cadence, 2) we provision a draft PO template back (attached) for you to slot values into, 3) finance confirms any Net60 approval timeline.

Thanks — attaching: SOW_Redwood_PO_Template.pdf (PDF, 120KB), pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (Excel, 56KB)

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Alicia — quick note from the SRE/ops handoff perspective: if you plan to request multiple billing entities (you mentioned two legal entities in the intake), we need to set entity-level billing at contract signature. That means separate billing entities create separate invoices (we can consolidate in reporting but not in the remit file).

If Sygnus wants a single consolidated remit, please confirm which legal entity will be the payer and we will route all charges there.

Also: pricing_grid_v3 has the committed-discount bands. For the 2% Net45 concession Ben mentioned, we require a 12-month committed ARR line in the SOW and a sign-off clause that ties the discount to maintained usage thresholds. I'll put a suggested clause into the SOW and share for your redlines.

Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement acceptance rules and invoice rhythm for Sygnus Labs

Alicia / team — Vivek here from Finance. A couple of clarifications from our side on Net terms / PO requirements that affect credit setup and billing cadence: 

1) Net60 requests: we require (a) a signed commercial agreement, (b) a credit application (we can accept the vendor-supplied form), and (c) one of the following: a letter of credit or a purchase order with a purchase order confirmation and an ERP supplier ID. Typical review time is 7-10 business days.

2) Invoice consolidation: for ERP matching we need the PO number on the invoice header and line items. If your ERP needs the internal cost center per-line we can include that if you supply the mapping up front; otherwise we will populate a free-form reference field.

3) Surcharge for per-PO invoicing: as Ben noted, operational surcharge applies; this is because we cannot batch token usage across invoices for accounting when multiple small PO numbers are present. We are open to a quarterly reconciliation approach if that helps — issue monthly small invoices and then a quarterly consolidated credit memo to reconcile variance.

If Sygnus is open to Net45 and a commitment threshold of $120k ARR, we can automate Net45 credit approval within 48 hours after agreement signature. Otherwise Net30 remains our default.

I can run the credit paperwork in parallel if you confirm intent.

Vivek Kulkarni
Finance Partner, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Thanks — this is very helpful. We reviewed the attachments and the proposed clauses. Confirming the following so we can move this to legal: 

- Sygnus will nominate Sygnus Labs, Inc. as the single paying entity for initial rollout.
- We are comfortable with monthly consolidated invoices per billing entity (one payer, one invoice).
- We will target Net45 with the 2% concession and a 12-month committed ARR of $125,000. Procurement will submit a credit application and the PO will include the required PO reference field and line-level cost-center mapping.

Action items:
- Ben / Vanessa: please send the SOW with the discount clause and a populated PO template reflecting the cost-center line mapping (Alicia will slot internal codes).
- Vivek: please confirm the expected credit review completion date once we submit the application (Alicia will aim to send the credit app by EOD Wednesday).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — will escalate internally if we need an earlier start date.

Alicia Mendez
